articles.title: BBC News app
articles.description: Top stories, breaking news, live reporting, and follow news topics that match your interests

articles.title: Brad Pitt stars as a tank commander on a dangerous mission in WWII
articles.description: Film following a battle-hardened US tank crew taking on the enemy’s brutal rearguard action

articles.title: Robert Pattinson on new film Primetime and how hunting predators became hit TV
articles.description: The actor portrays the real-life host of American TV show, To Catch a Predator, in his latest film.

articles.title: American ranchers wrestle with soaring costs - and their loyalty to Trump
articles.description: Many farmers in states that backed the president say they are being hit from all sides, with the crucial midterm elections just weeks away.

articles.title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president
articles.description: Brad Smith calls for global rules on AI, and says the UK is in the "best position" to lead the charge.

articles.title: Iran war threatens Healey's Budget plans, think tank warns
articles.description: The impact of the Iran war poses significant risks for the government’s spending plans, the Institute for Fiscal Studies says.

articles.title: Sacha Baron Cohen to star in Quentin Tarantino's West End play
articles.description: The Borat star said he was "beyond delighted" to be working on the show, The Popinjay Cavalier, with the Pulp Fiction director.

articles.title: Could you spot cancer symptoms in children?
articles.description: Although rare, cancer is the leading cause of death from disease among children under 15 in the UK.

articles.title: Ex-hurricane to bring warm weather to the UK this week
articles.description: Close to record-breaking warm nights are possible this week as warmer air heads for the UK.

articles.title: One killed, 11 injured in second Houthi strike on Riyadh airport in two days
articles.description: The Saudi capital has been hit by multiple attacks from the Iran-backed Yemeni group over the weekend.

articles.title: Trump's 'energy ceasefire' claim welcomed by Zelensky but Russia silent
articles.description: Ukraine's leader says he will support such a truce if Moscow does, after initially expressing surprise at Donald Trump's announcement.

articles.title: Reform would suspend asylum system for parliamentary term if in government
articles.description: All asylum applications would be rejected and existing ones voided, with all claimants marked for deportation.

articles.title: An Israeli Election Like No Other
articles.description: Many say a vote in two weeks may be the most consequential in Israel’s history.

articles.title: Pope Leo Will Have Surgery to Remove Growth on Lung
articles.description: A recent medical examination found a small nodule, he announced, adding that doctors would remove it this week.

articles.title: Man City's statement win has feeling of irrelevance with season in limbo
articles.description: Manchester City record what they will view as a statement win at Liverpool - but is it a statement that carries any weight during a Premier League season in limbo, asks Phil McNulty?

articles.title: Legoland Windsor evacuated over burst water main
articles.description: Some customers were forced to leave the theme park halfway through their visit on Sunday.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Has Few Options as Houthis Aim at Heart of Its Ambitions
articles.description: Three deadly attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen on an airport in the Saudi capital underscored the asymmetrical nature of their conflict with the kingdom.

articles.title: Winless and an 'easy touch' - what's happened to the Anfield fear factor?
articles.description: Liverpool's struggles at Anfield continue as Iraola still awaits his first Premier League win at Anfield.

articles.title: Orangutans released back into Borneo forest after devastating fires
articles.description: Rescuers moved the apes after their habitats were threatened by intense wildfires over the summer.

articles.title: Doku delights as Manchester City cruise past 10-man Liverpool
articles.description: In their first match since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules, Manchester City enjoyed a comfortable 3-0 win against Liverpool at Anfield to extend their perfect start to six matches, as they moved three points clear at the top of the Premier League.

articles.title: Over 100 Migrants Are Dead After Boat Capsizes Near Djibouti
articles.description: The shipwreck is among the deadliest ever recorded on the route to Yemen, the International Organization for Migration said. Dozens remain missing, and the bodies of 15 children were recovered.

articles.title: Hamilton apologises to Ferrari as Antonelli moves to brink of title
articles.description: Lewis Hamilton's incorrect strategy call during the Singapore Grand Prix means Kimi Antonelli can win the world title at the next race in Austin.

articles.title: Burnham to release details of Man City meetings
articles.description: Andy Burnham has faced criticism for comments he made in the wake of Manchester City being found guilty of all charges related to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.

articles.title: PM says it is 'clear' Russia interfered with Brexit vote
articles.description: He says voters were not "sufficiently" informed about how foreign actors sought to disrupt UK democracy.

articles.title: Ukraine Shrugs Off Trump Call to Ditch Zelensky for Energy Strikes
articles.description: President Trump lashed out at President Volodymyr Zelensky for striking Russian oil refineries. Mr. Zelensky said he’ll stop — if Russia does too.

articles.title: Sensational Smith, relentless quicks - Australia veterans serve reminder
articles.description: The fearsome pace quartet and Steve Smith's brilliance serves as a reminder of Australia's quality as the tourists take charge against South Africa.

articles.title: India’s Youth Protests Challenge Narendra Modi
articles.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India has long succeeded in isolating and undermining opponents. The Gen Z protests pose a challenge unlike any he has faced before.

articles.title: Poland detains man suspected of planning assassination of PM Tusk
articles.description: Police received credible information about possible attacks against Donald Tusk and his defence minister.

articles.title: Pakistan Seizes Control of an Opposition-Led Province
articles.description: The federal government, speaking of “a severe breakdown in law and order” in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid militant violence, named a politically allied official as in charge.

articles.title: India’s ‘Cockroach’ Leaders Released as Small Protests Go On in Delhi
articles.description: The leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party, an Indian youth movement, had been detained by the police on Saturday before they could lead protests over voting rights.

articles.title: Children among 139 dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
articles.description: The boat was travelling from Djibouti to Yemen with 305 people on board, when it capsized near the port town of Obock on Thursday night.

articles.title: Poland stabbings driven by online glorification of violence, Tusk says
articles.description: The PM was speaking after violent attacks at Polish schools this week left one dead and others injured.

articles.title: Ukraine strikes Yandex data centre in third attack on Russian tech giant
articles.description: It is the third time this week that Ukraine has targeted Russian tech giant Yandex, forcing the company to suspend its operations.

articles.title: Man Dies in Tiger Attack at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in England
articles.description: The man came face to face with an Amur tiger inside the animal’s habitat at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in England. The park was evacuated and closed to the public.

articles.title: Wildlife park remains closed after fatal tiger attack
articles.description: Yorkshire Wildlife Park remains closed after a man entered the tiger enclosure and was fatally attacked on Saturday.

articles.title: Wringing Hope From the Rubble of Gaza
articles.description: The cease-fire last October ostensibly brought an end to Israel’s war in Gaza after the Hamas-led attacks on Oct. 7, 2023. A year later, however, Israeli strikes, though less frequent, haven’t stopped.

articles.title: What to Know About the Protests in India
articles.description: Scattered protests against sweeping revisions to India’s voter rolls broke out on Sunday in New Delhi. The police met earlier protests with an extraordinary show of force.

articles.title: DUP MP says her party could help remove O'Neill as first minister over Drumcree row
articles.description: Carla Lockhart says unionist voters are angry at Michelle O'Neill over her role in the Garvaghy Road protests.

articles.title: Buildings swept away as flash floods hit central Nepal
articles.description: A flash flood at the Budhi Gandaki River has swept away several buildings and bridges, two months after catastrophic floods hit the country.

articles.title: In Canada’s Arctic, a New Generation of Inuit Creatives Are Using Identity to Fuel Their Art
articles.description: In Iqaluit, the only city in Canada’s Arctic, a new generation of Inuit writers and artists is turning questions of language, land and identity into books, films and even tattoos.

articles.title: A Russian Spy’s Lone Regret: ‘I Got Caught’
articles.description: Though born in Ukraine, Alexsander supports the Russian cause. He wishes he had deleted one photo from his phone.

articles.title: A Reporter Returns to China to Find it Richer, but Also Highly Paranoid.
articles.description: Returning to China after decades away, a correspondent finds bullet trains, dazzling skylines — and a surveillance state more paranoid and pervasive than ever.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh Airport Attacked Again, After Days of Houthi Strikes
articles.description: The strike on Saturday was the deadliest attack in a Gulf Arab country since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began in February, and forced the airport to temporarily suspend operations.

articles.title: Rebuking Ukraine Over Oil Strikes, Trump Says It Should ‘Get a New President’
articles.description: Hours after President Trump said the United States would buy Russian diesel, the Kremlin said there would be no immediate resumption of discussions to end the war.

articles.title: Quebec Independence Is Unlikely, but Some Will Still Dream
articles.description: The idea of independence remains deeply unpopular in Quebec, yet the separatist Parti Québécois was re-elected to a minority government this week.

articles.title: 3 Men Found Guilty in Murders of Tourists on Mexico Surf Trip
articles.description: The 2024 killings of two Australian brothers and their American friend drew international attention.

articles.title: Exasperation and Resignation in Greece Over Allegations Against Kimberly Guilfoyle
articles.description: The U.S. ambassador to Greece is facing accusations that she asked a donor to pay off her credit card bill before she took up her post in Athens.

articles.title: A Week Later, Russia Hasn’t Said What Pathogen Killed Plague Researcher
articles.description: Experts said they believed that with modern testing technology, the Russian authorities should know the answer by now.

articles.title: Palestinian Authority Formally Delays Elections, Despite Western Pressure
articles.description: The aging Palestinian leader, Mahmoud Abbas, pushed off the planned vote until late 2027. Palestinians haven’t had major elections for about two decades.

articles.title: Indian Police Round Up Protest Leaders and Lock Down Delhi
articles.description: Thousands of young people tried to gather to protest a sweeping revision of their country’s voter roll. Security forces hauled many of them away.
